deck_name: 君の名は。 Ch.4 探訪 — Vocabulary
source: 新海誠『君の名は。』(角川つばさ文庫), 第4章「探訪」
notes: 瀧 can no longer reach 三葉, so he sets out for Hida with 司 and 奥寺先輩, armed only with sketches of a landscape he remembers. A ramen shop owner identifies it as 糸守町, destroyed three years earlier when a comet fragment fell during its autumn festival; 瀧 faces the ruins, the newspaper archives and the list of the dead while his memories begin to slip. The deck focuses on searching and travel, rural Gifu, the disaster as news and historical record, shock and disbelief, and fading memory. The list is built from the chapter's scenes and the novel's style, not transcribed page by page, so a few words may sit a chapter early or late.

priority_guide.high: Learn before or while reading this chapter — it carries the scene.
priority_guide.medium: Useful; context usually helps if you forget it.
priority_guide.low: Recognition is enough — look it up once, don't over-drill.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 / literary — ambitious; learn to recognise it.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Rare kanji or irregular reading — learn the kana form first.

cards.scene: The chapter title — 瀧 sets out to visit the places in his memory and look for 三葉 in person.
cards.context: 探 (search) + 訪 (visit): going somewhere to investigate first-hand. Written register, common in titles such as 歴史探訪 or 町並み探訪 (local-history features); in speech you would say 探しに行く.
cards.example_sentence: 週末に、古い町並みを探訪するテレビ番組を見た。
cards.example_reading: しゅうまつ に、 ふるい まちなみ を たんぼう する テレビ ばんぐみ を みた。
cards.example_meaning: On the weekend I watched a TV programme exploring old streetscapes.

meanings: a guess from what one knows
cards.scene: 瀧 has no idea where 三葉 actually lives — and the people he later asks have none either.
cards.context: Almost always with ある/ない: 心当たりがある = 'I have an idea / that rings a bell'; 心当たりはありませんか is the standard question when asking around. Compare 手がかり (an outside clue) — 心当たり is something already in your own head.
cards.example_sentence: この写真の場所に心当たりはありませんか。
cards.example_reading: この しゃしん の ばしょ に こころあたり は ありません か。
cards.example_meaning: Do you have any idea where this photo was taken?

cards.scene: With no address and no way to contact her, 瀧's only clue is the landscape he remembers from living in 三葉's body.
cards.context: Also written 手掛かり — literally 'a handhold'. Collocations: 手がかりがない, 手がかりをつかむ (find a lead), 唯一の手がかり (the only clue). The key word of the whole search.
cards.example_sentence: 唯一の手がかりは、夢で見た湖の形だけだった。
cards.example_reading: ゆいいつ の てがかり は、 ゆめ で みた みずうみ の かたち だけ だった。
cards.example_meaning: The only clue was the shape of the lake he had seen in his dreams.

cards.scene: 瀧 draws the town's landscape from memory, sketch after sketch, before setting out.
cards.context: 描く can be read えがく or かく. Narration favours えがく, especially for depicting a scene or picturing something (心に描く); everyday 'draw a picture' is usually 絵をかく.
cards.example_sentence: 記憶の中の景色を、何枚も紙に描いた。
cards.example_reading: きおく の なか の けしき を、 なんまい も かみ に えがいた。
cards.example_meaning: He drew the scenery from his memory on sheet after sheet of paper.

meanings: row of houses along a street
cards.scene: 瀧's sketches show the lakeside town's streets, houses and hills — the view he hopes someone will recognise.
cards.context: 町 + 並み (a row, a line-up — as in 山並み mountain range, 家並み row of houses). Describes the overall look of a town's buildings: 古い町並み, 町並みを残す.
cards.example_sentence: 飛騨の古い町並みを歩くと、時間が止まったように感じる。
cards.example_reading: ひだ の ふるい まちなみ を あるく と、 じかん が とまった よう に かんじる。
cards.example_meaning: Walking through Hida's old streets, it feels as if time has stopped.

cards.scene: Fits 司 and 奥寺先輩's reaction to 瀧's sudden, hard-to-explain trip — doubtful, but they come along anyway.
cards.context: Four-character compound: half 信 (believe), half 疑 (doubt). Used as 半信半疑で聞く or 半信半疑のまま. Common in narration when someone hears an unlikely story.
cards.example_sentence: テッシーの話を、サヤちんは半信半疑で聞いていた。
cards.example_reading: テッシー の はなし を、 サヤちん は はんしんはんぎ で きいて いた。
cards.example_meaning: サヤちん listened to テッシー's story only half believing it.

cards.scene: From Tokyo the three ride the shinkansen and then change to a limited express heading into the Hida mountains.
cards.context: 乗る + 継ぐ (join on). Stresses carrying a journey on through connections: 新幹線と特急を乗り継ぐ. 乗り換える is the everyday 'change trains'; the noun 乗り継ぎ is also used for flight connections.
cards.example_sentence: 名古屋で特急に乗り継いで、山の方へ向かった。
cards.example_reading: なごや で とっきゅう に のりついで、 やま の ほう へ むかった。
cards.example_meaning: We changed to a limited express at Nagoya and headed toward the mountains.

meanings: view from a train or car window
cards.scene: On the train ride, the city gives way to mountains and rivers outside the window.
cards.context: 車 + 窓, literary. Usually refers to the scenery seen through it: 車窓の景色, 車窓から眺める. Everyday speech says 電車の窓から.
cards.example_sentence: 車窓には、どこまでも続く緑の山が広がっていた。
cards.example_reading: しゃそう に は、 どこ まで も つづく みどり の やま が ひろがって いた。
cards.example_meaning: Outside the train window, green mountains stretched on and on.

cards.scene: The trip takes the three to the Hida region, where 瀧 begins searching for the town in his sketches.
cards.context: An old province name, now the northern half of 岐阜県 (towns such as 高山 and 飛騨古川). 騨 is a rare kanji used almost only here. Itomori's speech in the story is modelled on 飛騨弁, the Hida dialect.
cards.example_sentence: 飛騨の山々は、秋になると赤や黄色に染まる。
cards.example_reading: ひだ の やまやま は、 あき に なる と あか や きいろ に そまる。
cards.example_meaning: The mountains of Hida turn red and yellow in autumn.

cards.scene: The search unfolds in Gifu Prefecture, the inland, mountainous setting of the fictional town.
cards.context: 阜 (mound) is rare outside this name — learn ぎふ as a unit. Gifu is landlocked; Hida is its northern half and 美濃 (みの) its southern half.
cards.example_sentence: 岐阜県には海がないが、川と山がとても美しい。
cards.example_reading: ぎふけん に は うみ が ない が、 かわ と やま が とても うつくしい。
cards.example_meaning: Gifu Prefecture has no coastline, but its rivers and mountains are beautiful.

cards.scene: The towns they pass through sit in narrow valleys between the Hida mountains.
cards.context: Also written 山間 (read やまあい; さんかん in compounds such as 山間部). Literary-sounding but common in travel writing: 山あいの村, 山あいを走る列車.
cards.example_sentence: 列車は山あいの小さな駅にゆっくり止まった。
cards.example_reading: れっしゃ は やまあい の ちいさな えき に ゆっくり とまった。
cards.example_meaning: The train slowly pulled into a small station among the mountains.

cards.scene: Rural Gifu looks calm and unhurried — a sharp contrast with the urgency 瀧 feels.
cards.context: Kanji 長閑 (rare — usually written in kana). Used for idyllic rural scenes and mild weather: のどかな田舎, のどかな春の日. It has no negative edge, unlike 退屈 (boring).
cards.example_sentence: 田んぼのそばを、のどかな風景を眺めながら歩いた。
cards.example_reading: たんぼ の そば を、 のどか な ふうけい を ながめ ながら あるいた。
cards.example_meaning: We walked beside the rice fields, taking in the peaceful scenery.

cards.scene: The three go from place to place showing 瀧's sketches and asking locals whether they know the town.
cards.context: From 聞き込む. Detective-drama vocabulary: 聞き込みをする, 聞き込み捜査. 瀧's search is essentially a one-man police canvass.
cards.example_sentence: 三人は駅前で絵を見せながら、聞き込みを続けた。
cards.example_reading: さんにん は えきまえ で え を みせ ながら、 ききこみ を つづけた。
cards.example_meaning: The three kept asking around in front of the station, showing the drawing.

cards.scene: They show the sketches to local people — shop staff, passers-by — hoping someone knows the place.
cards.context: 地元の人 = locals; 地元の店 = a local shop; also 'one's home town' (地元に帰る). Often contrasted with 観光客 (tourists).
cards.example_sentence: 地元の人なら、この山の名前を知っているはずだ。
cards.example_reading: じもと の ひと なら、 この やま の なまえ を しって いる はず だ。
cards.example_meaning: A local should know the name of this mountain.

meanings: the sense of having seen something before
cards.scene: Again and again people look at the drawings and nobody recognises the town — until the ramen shop.
cards.context: 見覚えがある/ない = 'looks familiar / doesn't look familiar'. Compare 聞き覚え (a voice or name that rings a bell). Unlike 既視感 (déjà vu), 見覚え is genuine recognition.
cards.example_sentence: この湖の形、どこかで見覚えがある。
cards.example_reading: この みずうみ の かたち、 どこか で みおぼえ が ある。
cards.example_meaning: The shape of this lake looks familiar from somewhere.

cards.scene: The locals who look at 瀧's sketches tilt their heads — they can't place the town.
cards.context: Kanji 首を傾げる. A gesture of puzzlement or doubt that appears constantly in Japanese narration. Figuratively, 首をかしげる means to find something questionable.
cards.example_sentence: おばあさんは絵をじっと見て、首をかしげた。
cards.example_reading: おばあさん は え を じっと みて、 くび を かしげた。
cards.example_meaning: The old woman stared at the picture and tilted her head, puzzled.

cards.scene: With nothing but drawings to go on, the three end up wandering without a real destination.
cards.context: 当て = something to rely on, a target (当てにする = count on). あてもなく歩く/さまよう = wander with no aim. Kanji form 当てもなく; close to 手がかりもなく but stressing the lack of a destination.
cards.example_sentence: 知らない町を、あてもなく一日中歩いた。
cards.example_reading: しらない まち を、 あて も なく いちにちじゅう あるいた。
cards.example_meaning: I wandered around a strange town aimlessly all day.

cards.scene: Hours of asking around bring no promising reaction at all.
cards.context: Literally the feel in your hand when something responds (a fish biting, a punch landing). 手応えがある = it feels like it's working; 手応えがない = getting nowhere. ごたえ is the sound-changed form of 応え (こたえ).
cards.example_sentence: 何人に聞いても、まったく手応えがなかった。
cards.example_reading: なんにん に きいて も、 まったく てごたえ が なかった。
cards.example_meaning: No matter how many people we asked, we got no response at all.

cards.scene: Each inquiry comes up empty, and the day starts to feel wasted.
cards.context: Baseball origin: 空 (empty) + 振り (swing). Used figuratively for efforts that produce nothing: 計画が空振りに終わる. Note 空 is read から here, not そら or くう.
cards.example_sentence: せっかく遠くまで来たのに、今日は空振りだった。
cards.example_reading: せっかく とおく まで きた のに、 きょう は からぶり だった。
cards.example_meaning: We came all this way, but today was a bust.

meanings: not to know what to do
to be at one's wits' end
cards.simpler_synonym: どうしたらいいかわからない
cards.scene: After the fruitless search, 瀧 has no idea what to do next.
cards.context: 途方 = a way or means; 暮れる = to grow dark, to come to an end — night falls on your options. A fixed expression used in both writing and speech.
cards.example_sentence: 最終バスが出てしまい、私たちは途方に暮れた。
cards.example_reading: さいしゅう バス が でて しまい、 わたしたち は とほう に くれた。
cards.example_meaning: The last bus had already left, and we were at a loss.

cards.scene: After hours of walking and asking, the three are worn out and hungry.
cards.context: 〜果てる = to the very end (see also 変わり果てる, 困り果てる). 疲れ果てた顔 = an exhausted face. Stronger and more literary than くたくた.
cards.example_sentence: 一日中歩き回って、すっかり疲れ果ててしまった。
cards.example_reading: いちにちじゅう あるきまわって、 すっかり つかれはてて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: After walking around all day, I was completely worn out.

cards.scene: After a day of fruitless asking, the three trudge on, tired and discouraged.
cards.context: とぼとぼ(と)歩く — slow, heavy steps of someone tired or disappointed. Compare てくてく (steady, neutral walking) and よろよろ (staggering).
cards.example_sentence: 試合に負けて、弟はとぼとぼと家に帰ってきた。
cards.example_reading: しあい に まけて、 おとうと は とぼとぼ と いえ に かえって きた。
cards.example_meaning: Having lost the match, my little brother trudged home.

cards.scene: At a ramen shop, the owner looks at 瀧's sketch and recognises the town.
cards.context: 店 + 主 (master). A narrative, written word; in speech you would say 店の人, ご主人, or 大将 for a ramen or sushi chef.
cards.example_sentence: ラーメン屋の店主は、絵を見て小さくうなずいた。
cards.example_reading: ラーメンや の てんしゅ は、 え を みて ちいさく うなずいた。
cards.example_meaning: The ramen shop owner looked at the picture and gave a small nod.

cards.scene: The owner explains that a piece split off from the comet as it passed Earth.
cards.context: 分 (divide) + 裂 (tear). Used for cells, comets and political parties: 核が分裂する, 党が分裂する. In the story, the comet's nucleus splitting is the cause of the disaster.
cards.example_sentence: 彗星の核が二つに分裂する様子が観測された。
cards.example_reading: すいせい の かく が ふたつ に ぶんれつ する ようす が かんそく された。
cards.example_meaning: The comet's nucleus was observed splitting in two.

cards.scene: It was a fragment of the comet that fell on the town, the owner explains.
cards.context: 破 (break) + 片 (piece). ガラスの破片 = shards of glass; 彗星の破片 = a comet fragment. Chapter 1's かけら is the soft, poetic cousin; 破片 is the factual, news-report word.
cards.example_sentence: 割れたガラスの破片で、指を切ってしまった。
cards.example_reading: われた ガラス の はへん で、 ゆび を きって しまった。
cards.example_meaning: I cut my finger on a shard of broken glass.

cards.scene: The fragment fell on Itomori during its autumn festival — the core fact of the disaster.
cards.context: The kango for 落ちる, used in news and science: 落下する, 落下物 (falling objects), 隕石の落下. 落下地点 = the point of impact. Note the sound change らく → らっ.
cards.example_sentence: 隕石の落下地点には、大きな穴ができていた。
cards.example_reading: いんせき の らっか ちてん に は、 おおきな あな が できて いた。
cards.example_meaning: A large hole had formed where the meteorite came down.

cards.scene: The fragment struck the town directly, in the middle of the festival.
cards.context: 直 (direct) + 撃 (strike). 台風が直撃する (a typhoon hits directly) is the everyday news use. Compared with 衝突 (two things colliding), 直撃 stresses a target being hit.
cards.example_sentence: 台風が町を直撃し、多くの家が壊れた。
cards.example_reading: たいふう が まち を ちょくげき し、 おおく の いえ が こわれた。
cards.example_meaning: The typhoon hit the town directly, and many houses were destroyed.

cards.scene: The owner tells them the town was wiped out — almost nothing was left.
cards.context: 壊 (break) + 滅 (perish). 壊滅する, 壊滅的な被害 (catastrophic damage). Stronger than 破壊 (destruction): 壊滅 means a whole community or system is gone.
cards.example_sentence: 地震で、その村は壊滅的な被害を受けた。
cards.example_reading: じしん で、 その むら は かいめつてき な ひがい を うけた。
cards.example_meaning: The earthquake caused catastrophic damage to the village.

cards.scene: Hundreds of people died, the owner says — the festival crowd became the disaster's victims.
cards.context: 犠牲 = sacrifice; 犠牲者 = people who lost their lives (or were harmed) in a disaster or accident. News register: 犠牲者は五百人を超えた. Both 犠 and 牲 contain 牛, from the sacrificial ox.
cards.example_sentence: 事故の犠牲者のために、町の人々は花を供えた。
cards.example_reading: じこ の ぎせいしゃ の ため に、 まち の ひとびと は はな を そなえた。
cards.example_meaning: The townspeople laid flowers for the victims of the accident.

cards.simpler_synonym: どこにいるかわからない
cards.scene: Part of the standard casualty language around the disaster — the dead and the missing.
cards.context: 行方 is read ゆくえ (irregular — not こうほう). 行方不明者 = missing person; news often pairs 死者・行方不明者. 行方 alone = whereabouts: 行方を探す.
cards.example_sentence: 山で行方不明になった男性が、三日後に見つかった。
cards.example_reading: やま で ゆくえふめい に なった だんせい が、 みっか ご に みつかった。
cards.example_meaning: The man who went missing in the mountains was found three days later.

cards.scene: The owner, and later the archives, describe the scale of the damage to the town.
cards.context: 被 (suffer) + 害 (harm). 被害を受ける (suffer damage), 被害が出る, 被害者 (victim). The opposite side is 加害者 (perpetrator).
cards.example_sentence: 大雨による被害は、町全体に広がった。
cards.example_reading: おおあめ に よる ひがい は、 まち ぜんたい に ひろがった。
cards.example_meaning: The damage from the heavy rain spread across the whole town.

cards.scene: From high ground, they look down over what remains of the town and its lakes.
cards.context: 見る + 下ろす. Physical: 丘から町を見下ろす. 'Look down on someone' (contempt) is usually 見下す (みくだす). Opposite: 見上げる.
cards.example_sentence: 丘の上から、湖と町を見下ろした。
cards.example_reading: おか の うえ から、 みずうみ と まち を みおろした。
cards.example_meaning: From the top of the hill I looked down on the lake and the town.

cards.scene: The town 瀧 remembers as full of life is now an empty ruin.
cards.context: 廃 (abandon, disuse) + 墟 (ruined site — a rare kanji). 廃墟と化す = to be reduced to ruins. Related: 廃校 (closed school), 廃線 (abandoned railway line).
cards.example_sentence: かつてにぎやかだった商店街は、今では廃墟になっている。
cards.example_reading: かつて にぎやか だった しょうてんがい は、 いま で は はいきょ に なって いる。
cards.example_meaning: The once-bustling shopping street is now in ruins.

cards.scene: The abandoned town lies silent, with no sign of life.
cards.context: ひっそり(と)する / ひっそりとした = hushed, with no people around: ひっそりとした町. ひっそり暮らす = live quietly, out of sight. Often paired with 静まり返る (fall completely silent).
cards.example_sentence: 人のいなくなった村は、ひっそりと静まり返っていた。
cards.example_reading: ひと の いなく なった むら は、 ひっそり と しずまりかえって いた。
cards.example_meaning: Emptied of people, the village lay hushed and silent.

cards.scene: The disaster zone is fenced off with no-entry signs.
cards.context: Signs usually drop the okurigana (立入禁止); running text writes 立ち入り禁止. 立ち入る = to enter a restricted place. Seen on fences, construction sites and rooftops.
cards.example_sentence: フェンスには「立入禁止」の看板がかかっていた。
cards.example_reading: フェンス に は 「たちいりきんし」 の かんばん が かかって いた。
cards.example_meaning: A 'No Entry' sign hung on the fence.

cards.scene: Part of the old town now lies underwater beside the lakes.
cards.context: 水 + 没 (sink, disappear). 水没する: 道路が水没する; casually, スマホが水没した = I dropped my phone in water. Common in flood reports.
cards.example_sentence: 大雨で、川沿いの道路が水没した。
cards.example_reading: おおあめ で、 かわぞい の どうろ が すいぼつ した。
cards.example_meaning: The riverside road went under water in the heavy rain.

cards.scene: Broken buildings and debris are all that remain of the streets 瀧 remembers.
cards.context: Kanji 瓦礫 (roof tile + pebble) — hard, so usually written がれき. Standard in disaster reporting: がれきの山 (heaps of rubble), がれきを撤去する (clear the rubble).
cards.example_sentence: 地震のあと、町はがれきの山になった。
cards.example_reading: じしん の あと、 まち は がれき の やま に なった。
cards.example_meaning: After the earthquake, the town became a mountain of rubble.

meanings: to be utterly transformed (for the worse)
cards.scene: The town 瀧 once walked through as 三葉 has been changed beyond recognition.
cards.context: 変わる + 果てる (to the extreme). Almost always negative: 変わり果てた町, 変わり果てた姿 (an unrecognisable, ruined figure — also used of the dead). A key emotional word for this scene.
cards.example_sentence: 久しぶりに見た故郷は、すっかり変わり果てていた。
cards.example_reading: ひさしぶり に みた こきょう は、 すっかり かわりはてて いた。
cards.example_meaning: Seen again after so long, my hometown had changed beyond recognition.

meanings: trace (of how something used to be)
lingering image (of a face or place)
cards.scene: Among the ruins, 瀧 searches for any trace of the town he knew.
cards.context: 面 (face) + 影 (shadow), read おもかげ. 昔の面影が残る = traces of the old days remain; 面影がない = unrecognisable. Also a person's lingering image: 母の面影. Poetic and very common in narration.
cards.example_sentence: 駅の周りには、昔の面影がまだ少し残っている。
cards.example_reading: えき の まわり に は、 むかし の おもかげ が まだ すこし のこって いる。
cards.example_meaning: Around the station, a few traces of the old days still remain.

cards.scene: Houses and streets 瀧 remembers have vanished without a trace.
cards.context: 跡形 = marks or traces left behind. Almost always with a vanishing verb: 跡形もなく消える / なくなる. Compare 跡地 (the site where something used to stand).
cards.example_sentence: 古い校舎は取り壊され、跡形もなく消えていた。
cards.example_reading: ふるい こうしゃ は とりこわされ、 あとかた も なく きえて いた。
cards.example_meaning: The old school building had been torn down and was gone without a trace.

cards.simpler_synonym: びっくりして何もできない
cards.scene: Standing in the ruins, 瀧 is too stunned to react.
cards.context: Usually 呆然とする or 呆然と立ち尽くす. 呆 is the same kanji as in 呆れる (be appalled). It describes the blank, emptied-out state after a shock; 愕然 is the sudden jolt itself.
cards.example_sentence: 結果を聞いて、彼はしばらく呆然としていた。
cards.example_reading: けっか を きいて、 かれ は しばらく ぼうぜん と して いた。
cards.example_meaning: Hearing the result, he stood stunned for a while.

cards.scene: The truth about the town hits 瀧 like a blow.
cards.context: 愕然とする. Stresses the sudden shock of discovering something terrible, whereas 呆然 is the daze that follows. 愕 (startle) is rare — learn the kana.
cards.example_sentence: 自分の間違いに気づいて、愕然とした。
cards.example_reading: じぶん の まちがい に きづいて、 がくぜん と した。
cards.example_meaning: I was aghast when I realised my mistake.

cards.scene: 瀧 stands rooted to the spot, staring at the ruined town.
cards.context: 立つ + 尽くす (exhaust). 〜尽くす means to do something completely; here, to stay standing, unable to move. Typical collocation: 呆然と立ち尽くす.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女は雨の中、何も言えずに立ち尽くしていた。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ は あめ の なか、 なにも いえず に たちつくして いた。
cards.example_meaning: She stood frozen in the rain, unable to say a word.

cards.scene: 瀧 insists he was talking with 三葉 only recently and grows frantic as his friends try to calm him.
cards.context: An emotional loss of control: 取り乱して叫ぶ; 取り乱してごめん = sorry I lost it. Opposites: 落ち着く, 冷静になる.
cards.example_sentence: 知らせを聞いた母は、取り乱して泣き出した。
cards.example_reading: しらせ を きいた はは は、 とりみだして なきだした。
cards.example_meaning: When my mother heard the news, she lost her composure and burst into tears.

cards.scene: Faced with a town gone for three years, the question hangs over 瀧: were his days with 三葉 real, or a phantom?
cards.context: まぼろし = something seen that is not really there, or something fleeting: 幻を見る, 幻のように消える. 幻の〜 can also mean 'legendary, almost impossible to find' (幻の名酒). Compare 夢 (dream) and 錯覚 (optical illusion).
cards.example_sentence: あの夏の出来事は、まるで幻だったように思える。
cards.example_reading: あの なつ の できごと は、 まるで まぼろし だった よう に おもえる。
cards.example_meaning: What happened that summer feels as if it were only an illusion.

cards.scene: The diary notes 三葉 left in 瀧's phone turn into garbled characters and vanish one by one.
cards.context: 文字 (characters) + 化ける (to transform, disguise oneself — as in お化け). The computer term for text displayed as nonsense symbols: 文字化けする. Here it is an eerie sign that the link between them is breaking.
cards.example_sentence: メールが文字化けして、何が書いてあるのか読めない。
cards.example_reading: メール が もじばけ して、 なに が かいて ある のか よめない。
cards.example_meaning: The email is garbled, and I can't read what it says.

cards.scene: The news hits 瀧 almost as hard as the impact that struck the town.
cards.context: Covers physical impact (衝撃波 = shock wave, 落下の衝撃) and emotional shock (衝撃を受ける, 衝撃的な事実). Both senses run through this chapter.
cards.example_sentence: その知らせに、クラス全員が衝撃を受けた。
cards.example_reading: その しらせ に、 クラス ぜんいん が しょうげき を うけた。
cards.example_meaning: The whole class was shocked by the news.

cards.scene: At the library, 瀧 reads how the disaster was reported three years earlier.
cards.context: 報 (report) + 道 (say). 報道する, 報道番組, 報道によると (according to reports). More formal than ニュース.
cards.example_sentence: 当時の報道によると、町の半分が被害を受けたという。
cards.example_reading: とうじ の ほうどう に よる と、 まち の はんぶん が ひがい を うけた と いう。
cards.example_meaning: According to reports at the time, half the town was damaged.

cards.scene: Newspaper headlines about the comet disaster fill the archive pages he searches.
cards.context: 見る + 出す: the part that catches the eye. 新聞の見出し, 大見出し (banner headline). 見出し語 = a dictionary headword.
cards.example_sentence: 新聞の一面には、大きな見出しで事故が伝えられていた。
cards.example_reading: しんぶん の いちめん に は、 おおきな みだし で じこ が つたえられて いた。
cards.example_meaning: The accident was reported on the front page under a big headline.

cards.scene: The newspapers show the town and the disaster as they were reported at the time, three years ago.
cards.context: 当時 points back to a specific past period: 当時の新聞, 当時は〜だった. Compare その頃 (conversational) and 現在 (the present).
cards.example_sentence: 当時の写真を見ると、町はとてもにぎやかだった。
cards.example_reading: とうじ の しゃしん を みる と、 まち は とても にぎやか だった。
cards.example_meaning: Judging from photos of the time, the town was very lively.

cards.scene: The records explain the comet's long orbit, which brings it back roughly every 1,200 years.
cards.context: 軌 (wheel track) + 道. 軌道を回る (to orbit), 軌道がずれる. Figurative: 軌道に乗る = to get on track (a business taking off).
cards.example_sentence: その彗星は長い軌道を回り、千年以上たってから戻ってくる。
cards.example_reading: その すいせい は ながい きどう を まわり、 せんねん いじょう たって から もどって くる。
cards.example_meaning: That comet travels a long orbit and returns only after more than a thousand years.

cards.scene: The records reveal that 糸守湖 itself was formed by a meteorite long ago.
cards.context: 隕 (fall from the sky — rare) + 石. 隕石が落ちる, 隕石湖 (meteorite lake), 隕石の衝突. A shooting star is 流れ星 or 流星; it only becomes a 隕石 when it reaches the ground.
cards.example_sentence: 博物館で、本物の隕石に触ることができた。
cards.example_reading: はくぶつかん で、 ほんもの の いんせき に さわる こと が できた。
cards.example_meaning: At the museum, I got to touch a real meteorite.

cards.scene: The lake, he reads, was created by an impact in the distant past.
cards.context: 太 (great) + 古 (old): further back than 昔 or 大昔, often prehistoric. 太古の昔, 太古から続く森. Literary register; don't confuse with 太鼓 (たいこ, drum).
cards.example_sentence: この森には、太古から続く静けさがある。
cards.example_reading: この もり に は、 たいこ から つづく しずけさ が ある。
cards.example_meaning: This forest holds a silence that has lasted since ancient times.

cards.scene: The records describe a town that, in effect, ceased to exist in a single night.
cards.context: 消 (vanish) + 滅 (perish). 町が消滅する, 消滅した村. More absolute than 消える: something is gone as an entity. Compare 壊滅 (destroyed) — a town can be 壊滅 and later 消滅 as a municipality.
cards.example_sentence: 人口が減り続け、その村はやがて消滅した。
cards.example_reading: じんこう が へりつづけ、 その むら は やがて しょうめつ した。
cards.example_meaning: Its population kept falling, and eventually the village ceased to exist.

cards.scene: The records count the town's residents who were lost in the disaster.
cards.context: 住 (live) + 民 (people). 住民票 (residence certificate), 地域住民 (local residents). News and administrative register; in speech, 町の人.
cards.example_sentence: 住民の多くは、祭りの会場に集まっていた。
cards.example_reading: じゅうみん の おおく は、 まつり の かいじょう に あつまって いた。
cards.example_meaning: Many of the residents had gathered at the festival grounds.

cards.scene: The list of the dead runs on in long columns of names, and among them 瀧 finds the ones he knows.
cards.context: ずらり(と)並ぶ = lined up in a long row (names, shops, bottles, people). Casual variant ずらっと. A visual mimetic, not a sound.
cards.example_sentence: 本棚には古い新聞がずらりと並んでいた。
cards.example_reading: ほんだな に は ふるい しんぶん が ずらり と ならんで いた。
cards.example_meaning: Old newspapers were lined up in long rows on the shelves.

cards.scene: 瀧 finds the list of the dead — and on it 三葉's name, along with her grandmother, sister and friends.
cards.context: 名 + 簿 (register, ledger — as in 帳簿). クラス名簿 (class roster), 犠牲者名簿 (list of victims), 名簿に載る (to be on a list).
cards.example_sentence: 犠牲者の名簿の中に、知っている名前を見つけた。
cards.example_reading: ぎせいしゃ の めいぼ の なか に、 しって いる なまえ を みつけた。
cards.example_meaning: I found a name I knew on the list of victims.

cards.scene: 瀧's memories and the dates in the records don't match — they are three years apart.
cards.context: From 食い違う (like teeth that don't meet). 話の食い違い = conflicting accounts; 意見の食い違い = a disagreement. The time difference between countries is 時差 — a different idea entirely.
cards.example_sentence: 二人の話には、いくつか食い違いがあった。
cards.example_reading: ふたり の はなし に は、 いくつか くいちがい が あった。
cards.example_meaning: There were several discrepancies between their two accounts.

cards.scene: The gap is in time itself: the 三葉 瀧 knew was living three years earlier than he was.
cards.context: From ずれる (to slip out of place). 時間のずれ, 感覚のずれ, 三年のずれ. Usually written in kana.
cards.example_sentence: スマホの日付と実際の日付に、ずれがあった。
cards.example_reading: スマホ の ひづけ と じっさい の ひづけ に、 ずれ が あった。
cards.example_meaning: There was a gap between the date on the phone and the actual date.

cards.scene: Once 瀧 sees the three-year gap, things that never made sense — like why he could never reach her — suddenly add up.
cards.context: Kanji 辻褄 (hard, usually written in kana). Lives in fixed phrases: つじつまが合う (it adds up), つじつまが合わない (it doesn't add up), つじつまを合わせる (make a story consistent, often by fudging).
cards.example_sentence: 彼の説明は、どうしてもつじつまが合わなかった。
cards.example_reading: かれ の せつめい は、 どうしても つじつま が あわなかった。
cards.example_meaning: His explanation just didn't add up, however you looked at it.

cards.scene: Realising what the three-year gap means sends a chill through 瀧.
cards.context: ぞっとする = a shiver of horror or disgust down your spine. 考えただけでぞっとする = the mere thought gives me chills. Compare ゾクゾク (shivers — which can also be excitement).
cards.example_sentence: もしあの時電車に乗っていたらと思うと、ぞっとする。
cards.example_reading: もし あの とき でんしゃ に のって いたら と おもう と、 ぞっと する。
cards.example_meaning: It sends a chill down my spine to think what would have happened if I'd been on that train.

cards.scene: Reading the archives, 瀧 grasps the terrible truth about when 三葉 lived.
cards.context: Stronger and more literary than 気づく: grasping something fundamental, often painful (死を悟る, 真実を悟る). Religious sense: 悟りを開く = attain enlightenment.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女の目を見て、もう会えないのだと悟った。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ の め を みて、 もう あえない の だ と さとった。
cards.example_meaning: Looking into her eyes, I realised I would never see her again.

cards.scene: The three spend the night at an inn after the library.
cards.context: やど = any lodging, often with a traditional feel: 宿を取る (book a room), 宿に泊まる. In compounds the reading is しゅく (宿泊, 下宿). 旅館 is specifically a Japanese-style inn.
cards.example_sentence: 日が暮れる前に、駅の近くで宿を探した。
cards.example_reading: ひ が くれる まえ に、 えき の ちかく で やど を さがした。
cards.example_meaning: We looked for somewhere to stay near the station before it got dark.

meanings: to be on the tip of one's tongue
cards.simpler_synonym: もう少しで思い出せる
cards.scene: At the inn, 三葉's name keeps almost coming back to 瀧 — and slipping away again.
cards.context: Literally 'to come out as far as the throat'. 名前が喉まで出かかっている = I almost have it. 出かかる = 出る + 〜かかる (be on the point of).
cards.example_sentence: あの歌手の名前が喉まで出かかっているのに、思い出せない。
cards.example_reading: あの かしゅ の なまえ が のど まで でかかって いる のに、 おもいだせない。
cards.example_meaning: That singer's name is on the tip of my tongue, but I can't recall it.

cards.scene: By that night, 瀧's memories of 三葉 have grown hazy and hard to hold on to.
cards.context: Kanji 朧げ (rare). From 朧 (hazy — as in 朧月, a misty moon). おぼろげな記憶, おぼろげに覚えている. Softer and more poetic than 曖昧 (ambiguous).
cards.example_sentence: 子どもの頃に住んでいた家のことは、おぼろげにしか覚えていない。
cards.example_reading: こども の ころ に すんで いた いえ の こと は、 おぼろげ に しか おぼえて いない。
cards.example_meaning: I only dimly remember the house I lived in as a child.

cards.scene: The harder 瀧 tries to hold on, the more his memories of 三葉 fade.
cards.context: From 薄い (thin, faint). 記憶が薄れる, 関心が薄れる, 痛みが薄れる. A gradual weakening — it pairs naturally with 〜ていく and 〜につれて.
cards.example_sentence: 時間がたつにつれて、その日の記憶は薄れていった。
cards.example_reading: じかん が たつ に つれて、 その ひ の きおく は うすれて いった。
cards.example_meaning: As time passed, the memory of that day faded.

cards.scene: Pieces of 瀧's memories — even her name — seem to drop out of his head.
cards.context: 抜ける + 落ちる. Physical: 髪が抜け落ちる. Figurative: 記憶がすっぽり抜け落ちる (a whole chunk of memory is gone); すっぽり is its typical partner.
cards.example_sentence: 事故の前後の記憶が、すっぽり抜け落ちている。
cards.example_reading: じこ の ぜんご の きおく が、 すっぽり ぬけおちて いる。
cards.example_meaning: My memory of the time around the accident is completely gone.

cards.scene: 瀧 makes up his mind to go alone to the shrine's sacred site on the mountain.
cards.context: 決意する, 決意を固める (firm up one's resolve). Weightier than 決める; close to 決心, but 決意 sounds more formal and steely.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は一人で山へ向かう決意をした。
cards.example_reading: かれ は ひとり で やま へ むかう けつい を した。
cards.example_meaning: He resolved to head into the mountains alone.
